decisions.reason: As a decorative devoré fabric line it builds directly on the firm's established interior-textile design, sampling and stocking capabilities, so management is likely to retain it and refine variants rather than withdraw it.

Transparent burnout decorative fabric is close to the firm's core decoration-textile knowledge, although some fashion sensitivity and overlap with related lines make it somewhat more vulnerable than the strongest core products.

This burnout decorative fabric fits existing know-how, but as a narrower offer beside other burnout/devoré launches it is the most exposed to assortment rationalisation if customer learning shows weaker differentiation.

A velour-like upholstery fabric is highly consistent with the firm's upholstery-textile business and customer base, so absorptive capacity and established service routines make continued marketing the most likely choice.

The flame-retardant inbetween fabric is adjacent to the firm's curtain and interior-textile activities, but the more specialised specification raises the chance of exit if demand stays niche or certification-related effort is not rewarded.

A polyester lining fabric complements the firm's made-to-measure sewing and dependable supply model, so it is likely to be kept, though it is somewhat less central to the design-led core than visible face fabrics.
